1.title: Controlling Cloud Costs
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Controlling Cloud Costs. It covers the exam area six. Scaling with Google Cloud operations. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. six point one Recognize how Google Cloud supports an organization's ability to control their cloud costs: the shift from capital expenditure to operational expenditure and its effect on total cost of ownership. Google-recommended practices for cloud financial governance. People, process and technology. The resource hierarchy. Controlling consumption with resource quota policies, budget threshold rules, Cloud Billing reports, Dynamic Workload Scheduler and spot V Ms. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: six. Scaling with Google Cloud operations (about ten percent). Exam format: ninety minutes and fifty to sixty multiple-choice questions. Validated against: the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide.

1.title: CapEx, OpEx and TCO
1.text: cap ex, op ex and T C O (total cost of ownership). Capital expenditure (cap ex). Large upfront spending on hardware and data centers. Operational expenditure (op ex). Ongoing pay-as-you-go spending on services. Total cost of ownership (T C O). All costs over time: hardware, space, power, staff, licenses, maintenance. Moving to the cloud shifts cap ex to op ex: no big upfront purchase, pay for use, scale spending with demand. T C O often falls because the company stops paying for idle capacity, data centers and much of the operations work. Exam tip: Cloud equals from cap ex to op ex. T C O is the whole cost, not only the price of servers.

1.title: Cloud financial governance
1.text: Cloud financial governance. Financial governance gives predictability and control over cloud costs. Identify who manages cloud costs. A named owner or team (often called Fin Ops). Use Google Cloud's cost management tools. Billing reports, budgets, alerts, quotas. People, process and technology. People share cost accountability; processes review and approve spend; technology measures and automates controls.

1.title: Cloud financial governance, continued
1.text: Cloud financial governance. The figure shows this: Costs are controlled with structure, limits, visibility and discounts.

1.title: The resource hierarchy
1.text: The resource hierarchy. Organization node. The root of the company's resources. Folders. Group projects by team, department or environment. Projects. The basic container for resources, billing and A P Is. Resources. Virtual machines, storage buckets, databases and so on. Access control. Grant access at a level; it is inherited downward. Inheritance and propagation. Policies flow from parents to children. Security and compliance. One place to set rules for many projects. Visibility and auditing. See and report costs and activity by folder or project.

1.title: Controlling consumption
1.text: Controlling consumption. Resource quota policies. Limit how much of a resource can be used (prevents runaway use). Budget threshold rules. Alert people when spending reaches set percentages of a budget. Cloud Billing reports. Visualize costs by project, product or label. Dynamic Workload Scheduler. Gets accelerator capacity, such as G P Us and T P Us, for A I and batch jobs with flexible scheduling to cost less. Spot V Ms. Discounted capacity that can be stopped, for fault-tolerant work. Exam tip: Quotas limit use. Budgets alert on spend. Billing reports show where money goes. A budget alert does not stop spending by itself. Exam tip: Cost words in a question: upfront versus ongoing equals cap ex and op ex, alert on spend equals budget, limit use equals quota, see where money goes equals billing reports, cheaper interruptible capacity equals spot V Ms.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company stops buying servers and instead pays monthly for the resources it uses. What shift is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: From cap ex to op ex, with pay-as-you-go costs. Moving to the cloud replaces large upfront capital spending with ongoing operational spending.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which measure includes hardware, power, staff, licenses and maintenance over time? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Total cost of ownership. Total cost of ownership counts all costs over time, not only purchase prices.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A finance team wants an email when spending reaches eighty percent of the monthly plan. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A budget threshold rule. Budget threshold rules alert people when spending reaches set percentages of a budget.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A company wants to prevent one project from creating an unlimited number of virtual machines. Which control fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A resource quota policy that limits the use. Quota policies limit how much of a resource can be consumed.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company wants to give a team access to all of its projects at once and have the rules inherited by new projects. Where should access be set? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: On a folder in the resource hierarchy. Access set on a folder flows down to the projects and resources inside it.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which people-process-technology practice is part of cloud financial governance? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Identifying who manages cloud costs and reviewing spend. Financial governance names an owner for costs and uses processes and tools to review spend.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does moving to the cloud change about spending? Answer: cap ex becomes op ex. Question two. What does T C O include? Answer: All costs over time. Question three. What do budget threshold rules do? Answer: Alert at set percentages of a budget.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What do quotas do? Answer: Limit how much of a resource can be used. Question five. Name the resource hierarchy levels. Answer: Organization, folders, projects, resources. Question six. What are spot V Ms good for? Answer: Fault-tolerant work at a discount.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Finance: cap ex to op ex; T C O is total cost. Governance: owner for costs; people, process, technology. Hierarchy: organization, folders, projects, resources; inheritance. Controls: quotas (limit), budgets (alert), billing reports (see), D W S and spot V Ms (cheaper capacity).
